3.speaker: Katarina Horten
3.text: "So, Mr. President... You are not willing to resign, but willing to talk to the protesters..."

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: She was a rising figure in Sordish politics, especially due to her involvement in organizing the largest women's marches.

5.speaker: Katarina Horten
5.text: "Let me remind you, this is not a regular protest. This is a movement."

6.speaker: Katarina Horten
6.text: "People are finally calling out for the change they've been denied for so long. Your administration and your party left them no choice."

7.speaker: Player
7.text: "Just make your point. You are falling into diatribe."

8.speaker: Player
8.text: "People? How about you? What do you earn from inciting unrest?"

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: It seemed like she was navigating the protests very cleverly and knew how to make people come together. She had somehow become the spokesperson for these massive "Soll Square Protests" against me.

11.speaker: Player
11.text: "I respect that, Mrs. Horten. That's why we're here to have a discussion."

12.speaker: Katarina Horten
12.text: "Did you even look at these people, Mr. President?"

16.speaker: Player
16.text: "What you are doing is illegal. We are in an emergency."

17.speaker: Katarina Horten
17.text: "This is precisely why we had to speak out, Mr. President."

18.speaker: Katarina Horten
18.text: "You cannot take away the right to protest. This is an infringement on our basic rights as citizens of this country."

19.speaker: Katarina Horten
19.text: "You are getting this all wrong, Mr. President. I do not *earn* anything from this..."

21.speaker: Katarina Horten
21.text: "You think they cannot distinguish right from wrong? That they always need a leader figure to organize?"

22.speaker: Katarina Horten
22.text: "You are tremendously wrong. You must accept that people do not support you anymore, Mr. President. You've done wrong by them. By all of us."

25.speaker: Katarina Horten
25.text: "Maybe your values are different from what they want."

27.speaker: Katarina Horten
27.text: "You brought people from all walks of life together. People you'd never think would come together."

28.speaker: Katarina Horten
28.text: "But they did. This is a huge achievement. I can at least give you credit for that."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: "I've seen them, Mrs. Horten. And I want to help."

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "Nonsense. They are coming together because of people like you."

31.speaker: Katarina Horten
31.text: "You already know about the issues that made people take to the streets."

32.speaker: Katarina Horten
32.text: "We don't believe you can fix them anymore. That's why they're asking for your resignation."

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: She looked at me with a single arched eyebrow.

34.speaker: Katarina Horten
34.text: "But I don't think that's going to happen. Nor it is helpful at this moment. Elections are getting close anyway."

36.speaker: Player
36.text: "You can't blame the actions of a couple of policeman on the whole state. Nor on me."

37.speaker: Katarina Horten
37.text: "Instead, I want you to make amends."

38.speaker: Katarina Horten
38.text: "When peaceful protesters went out to Soll Square to voice their opinion a few weeks ago, your police nearly beat them to death."

39.speaker: Katarina Horten
39.text: "This isn't about your policies anymore. This is about democracy and the fundamental right to be free. To be safe."

40.speaker: Katarina Horten
40.text: "The police state Soll created still lives on. Every president who takes the seat feels obliged to use that force. It needs to stop."

41.speaker: Katarina Horten
41.text: "The problem isn't their funding. It goes deeper than that."

42.speaker: Player
42.text: "These policemen acted on their own accord. We never gave them such orders."

43.speaker: Player
43.text: "I've already defunded the police. What more can I do?"

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "I'm ready to do something about this."

49.speaker: Katarina Horten
49.text: "You might not have given such orders, but the police feels that they have the right to partake in such actions. And they do not suffer any consequences for it."

51.speaker: Katarina Horten
51.text: "The problem is a systemic one. The police feels that they have the right to partake in such actions. And they do not suffer any consequences for it."

52.speaker: Katarina Horten
52.text: "We want those responsible to be tried. We want justice to be served."

53.speaker: Katarina Horten
53.text: "Firstly, we want the dismissal of Karl Greiser, the Chief of Police, for his use of excessive force..."

57.speaker: Katarina Horten
57.text: "When peaceful protesters went out to Soll Square to voice their opinion a few weeks ago, your police beat people to their deaths!"

58.speaker: Katarina Horten
58.text: "This isn't about any of your other policies anymore. You finally formed your police state. This is about democracy and the fundamental right to be free. To be safe."

59.speaker: Katarina Horten
59.text: "The police state Soll created lives on more powerful than ever. Every president who takes the seat feels obliged to use that force. It needs to stop."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "I'm ready to do something about this."

61.speaker: Player
61.text: "These policemen acted on their own accord. We never gave them such orders."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "You can't blame the actions of a couple of policeman on the whole state. Nor on me."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "Sordland had serious security problems. These laws were necessary."

65.speaker: Katarina Horten
65.text: "You gave them more authority than ever. How are you denying your part in this?"

69.speaker: Katarina Horten
69.text: "So, you are fine with killing your own citizens?"

71.speaker: Katarina Horten
71.text: "We must start by undoing your security laws."

73.speaker: Katarina Horten
73.text: "...And we demand that your harsher security laws be undone."

74.speaker: Katarina Horten
74.text: "...And we demand that Tarquin Soll's security package laws be undone."

75.speaker: Katarina Horten
75.text: "We worked together with the independent MPs on a new Freedom Act."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "I can help you with these. What is in this Freedom Act?"

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "I can't dismiss Mr. Greiser just like that. He was doing his job."

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: A muscle in her jaw twitched.

81.speaker: Katarina Horten
81.text: "You will continue the traditions of not giving a damn about the people!?"

82.speaker: Katarina Horten
82.text: "You seem not to understand the situation, Mr. President."

83.speaker: Katarina Horten
83.text: "We know what your powers are. And these are the people's demands."

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "This country still has a functioning government. I can't listen to the demands of every mob."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "I'm sorry, Mrs. Horten. But I can't do it. You need to compromise."

87.speaker: Katarina Horten
87.text: "I thought you invited me here to make compromises."

88.speaker: Katarina Horten
88.text: "The people have made many compromises, Mr. President. They stayed silent for decades. Now, it is your turn."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "You might be right... What's in this Freedom Act?"

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "I think they are being manipulated by people like you, Mrs. Horten. I doubt that these are their genuine demands."

91.speaker: Player
91.text: "I'm the president, Mrs. Horten. And I made my decision."

92.speaker: Player
92.text: "Be careful with your tone, Mrs. Horten. You are speaking to the president."

95.speaker: Katarina Horten
95.text: "Firstly, no person will be detained without proper trial."

99.speaker: Katarina Horten
99.text: "You must end the state of emergency now."

100.speaker: Katarina Horten
100.text: "We demand that you return from this mistake and respect our democracy."

101.speaker: Katarina Horten
101.text: "We also demand the dismissal of Karl Greiser, the Chief of Police, for his use of excessive force..."

106.speaker: Katarina Horten
106.text: "Investigating private property will require warrants issued by judges."

107.speaker: Katarina Horten
107.text: "The loopholes that give the police the right to use excessive force will be removed."

108.speaker: Katarina Horten
108.text: "And the police's right to stop and frisk anyone will be taken away."

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "Okay, I agree to all of your demands. I'll sign it."

113.speaker: Player
113.text: "Okay, I agree to all of your demands. I'll support your bill too. And I promise to sign it if it passes the Assembly."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "No. That is too much to ask."

116.speaker: Katarina Horten
116.text: "You cannot think clearly, Mr. President. You are losing it all."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "I'm not losing anything. But you'll lose something if you continue speaking to me like that."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "I care about the people, Mrs. Horten. But politics is more complicated than that."

122.speaker: Katarina Horten
122.text: "What's complicated about the tyranny of the state?"

123.speaker: Katarina Horten
123.text: "You are a fake. And you claim to be a socialist. You tried portraying yourself as a supporter of the working class."

130.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
130.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_WeakWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_StrongWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false

131.speaker: Katarina Horten
131.text: "You are a fake. And you tried portraying yourself as a supporter of women."
131.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Archetype_ComradeRayne"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_WeakWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_StrongWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true)

133.speaker: Katarina Horten
133.text: "You are a fake. You are no democrat. You tried portraying yourself as the champion of the people."
133.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Archetype_ComradeRayne"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_WeakWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn09_StrongWomensRights_Signed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_PresiPower_Default_GenderEqualityInEducation"] == true) == false)

134.speaker: Player
134.text: "Guards! Show Mrs. Horten the way out."

142.speaker: Player
142.text: "The meeting is over, Mrs. Horten. Please don't embarrass yourself further."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: She looked at me one last time and quickly walked towards the door.

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: The guards immediately came inside and took her by the arms.

150.speaker: Katarina Horten
150.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn08_HarsherSecurity_Signed"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn08_HarsherSecurity_Signed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn08_ExtendEmergency_Extend"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn08_ExtendEmergency_Extend"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_Censored"] == false) == false)

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: We went through the documents and discussed how we would proceed.

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: After we settled on our next actions, I signed the necessary papers and gave them to her.

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: As soon as we were done, she immediately stood up and bowed her head.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: The guards immediately came inside and took her by the arms.

205.speaker: Katarina Horten
205.text: "So, Mr. President... It's been a while."

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: Since our last confrontation, Katarina had become a rising figure in Sordish politics, organizing large women's marches as well as the massive "Soll Square Protests" against me.

210.speaker: Katarina Horten
210.text: "When you spoke in front of the Gasom headquarters, you made it seem as if we were on the same side."

211.speaker: Katarina Horten
211.text: "Did you learn nothing from our protests in Narbel? You cannot silence the people of Sordland, President Rayne. No matter how hard you try."

212.speaker: Katarina Horten
212.text: "Did you mean any of what you said back then?"

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "I did. And I still do. We are on the same side, Ms. Horten."

214.speaker: Player
214.text: "Times and positions change, Ms. Horten. If you want to enter politics, that's the first thing you should know."

215.speaker: Player
215.text: "Your people had me in a corner, Ms. Horten. I had to lie if I wanted to get out of there alive."

216.speaker: Player
216.text: "Did *you* learn anything, Ms. Horten? Speak against the President of Sordland, and you'll meet the wrong end of a nightstick."

217.speaker: Player
217.text: "My aim has never been to silence the people of Sordland. I'm here talking to you, aren't I?"

218.speaker: Player
218.text: "What I learned in Narbel is that the President of Sordland will face criticism even if he is trying to do everything right."

219.speaker: Katarina Horten
219.text: "You're not trying very hard, Mr. President."

220.speaker: Katarina Horten
220.text: "That's the very least you can do, Mr. President. Especially after having my colleague Mr. Stahler arrested."

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: She flinched in shock, then quickly recomposed herself.

223.speaker: Katarina Horten
223.text: "That's a cop-out, Mr. President. You have knowingly compromised the ideals you expressed to me back then."

228.speaker: Katarina Horten
228.text: "That's the very least you can do, Mr. President."

232.speaker: Katarina Horten
232.text: "You weren't trying very hard when you had my colleague Mr. Stahler arrested."

236.speaker: Katarina Horten
236.text: "You dare to say that after what you did to Mr. Stahler?"

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: It seemed like she was navigating the protests very cleverly and knew how to make people come together. She had somehow become the spokesperson for these massive "Maroon Square Protests" against me.

244.speaker: Katarina Horten
244.text: "When peaceful protesters went out to Maroon Square to voice their opinion a few weeks ago, your police nearly beat them to death."

248.speaker: Katarina Horten
248.text: "When peaceful protesters went out to Maroon Square to voice their opinion a few weeks ago, your police beat people to their deaths!"

252.text: Since our last confrontation, Katarina had become a rising figure in Sordish politics, organizing large women's marches as well as the massive "Maroon Square Protests" against me.
